title: WISE band signals require at least 1.06 percent dust power in G4466 under the adopted calibration and stellar template
abstract: We test the infrared energy demand of the dwarf dimmer G4466 without a smooth dust spectrum. Positive-spectrum optimization of the published WISE W3 and W4 signals gives a sharp lower apparent dust fraction of 1.2118 percent at the nominal signals, or 1.0638 percent after subtraction of two reported flux errors per band. A continuous dual certificate and two narrow spectral components establish the bound for the adopted photon-response interpolation. The errors are sensitivity inputs, not confidence limits. For the published 13-Jupiter-mass Roche-lobe example, at least 72.3 percent of isotropic passive emission must come from outside the lobe. An earlier exclusion with a fourfold directional factor does not survive the wider spectral class and these errors. This does not establish a physical confined-cloud solution. The stellar template, nominal instrument response, weak W4 signal, angular emission and source attribution limit the inference. No new photometry is used. Code, aggregate results, exact source hashes and external-scratch retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Minimum apparent dust power from WISE band signals, with no smooth-spectrum assumption. Error subtraction is a sensitivity parameter. Lobe ceilings use the published mass and orbit assumptions.
